abstract: A graph is vertex-transitive if, for any two vertices, there is an automorphism mapping one to the other. We prove that every connected vertex-transitive graph of order $p^n$, where $p$ is a prime and $p^n\geq 3$, has a hamiltonian cycle. Our main tool extends Witte's theorem [JCTB (1986)] on Cayley digraphs of $p$-groups.
hook: Every connected vertex-transitive graph with a prime-power number of vertices has a Hamilton cycle.
summary: A vertex-transitive graph looks the same from every vertex. The authors prove that any connected one with p^n vertices, at least 3, has a cycle visiting each vertex once. They do this by extending Witte's 1986 theorem on Cayley digraphs of p-groups. It covers prime-power orders only, so the general question for all orders stays open.
title: Hamilton cycles in vertex-transitive graphs of prime-power order
